CUSTOMER-FIRST
At ICICI Prudential AMC, we believe that consistent performance remains central to building enduring investor trust. In a market where investors increasingly have multiple choices across active and passive strategies, our focus continues to remain on delivering disciplined investment outcomes through market cycles.

In an industry built on fiduciary responsibility, trust is earned through consistent actions and long-term alignment with favourable investment outcomes. As of March 31, 2026, we serve a growing community of over 17 million, reflecting the growing trust placed in us by households across the country. Over the past year, we have welcomed 2.4 million new investors, with a meaningful proportion being first time participants in mutual funds. NAMTECH School of Social Impact The NAMTECH International Professional Technician Certificate Programme (iPTCP), supported by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited (the AMC) and monitored by ICICI Foundation for Inclusive Growth, was implemented by NAMTECH to enhance the employability of Industrial Training Institute (ITI) students by equipping them with industry-relevant technical competencies. Prabal Super 50 Programme

Prabal Super 50 Programme
ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd. through ICICI Foundation for Inclusive Growth, supported the Prabal Super 50 Programme implemented in collaboration with the Indian Army and Centre for Social Responsibility and Leadership (CSRL), aimed at providing free residential coaching for JEE preparation to children of Army personnel. The program offered academic coaching, mentoring support, study materials, mock tests, computer laboratory facilities, career guidance, and accommodation and boarding support to the beneficiaries. The programme supported 39 students, out of which 20 students qualified JEE Mains and 2 students qualified JEE Advanced. The impact assessment findings indicated improvement in students’ conceptual understanding, confidence levels, access to affordable coaching support, and reduced financial burden on families through the residential coaching model.
The intervention focused on bridging the gap between conventional vocational education and evolving industrial requirements by integrating hands-on technical learning with digital literacy, communication skills, and workplace readiness. The project covered a total of 725 beneficiaries across key trades including Industrial Automation, Automotive Technology (EV), and Advanced Welding across ITI Mehsana, ITI Vadnagar, and ITI Kheralu.

Management Discussion & Analysis
ECONOMIC OVERVIEW Global Economy The global economy showed stability in 2025 by successfully managing changing trade policies and different regional outcomes. Technology investments helped balance the effects of new tariffs and shifting policy directions. Global inflation reached a steady 4.1% as several countries reported figures that were lower than initial market expectations. Household consumption grew steadily worldwide in 2025, fuelled by technology investments and wage gains in key regions. In the United States and emerging Asia, spending on goods and services picked up as financial conditions eased, helping counter tariff impacts.

Trade tensions remained a key source of uncertainty during the period, as the legal status of US tariff actions and the future of related bilateral arrangements became less certain following the Supreme Court ruling that struck down the tariffs. This development added to the unpredictability around future tariff rates, trade policy direction, and the durability of recent bilateral understandings. Policy uncertainty remained elevated, even as businesses continued to adjust to the changing trade environment. Financial conditions stayed broadly supportive overall, while artificial intelligence-related investment and wider technology spending continued to provide an important offset to trade-related headwinds.
(Source: World Economic Outlook (IMF), WEO (IMF)-April)

(Source: World Economic Outlook (IMF), WEO (IMF)-April)
The geopolitical environment continues to remain uncertain, with heightened tensions in West Asia emerging as a key source of disruption to global trade, energy flows, and supply chains. While the Russia-Ukraine conflict continues to have residual effects on crude oil supply/price, commodity markets and logistics, the current focus of global risk has increasingly shifted towards West Asia, where escalating instability is contributing to supply-side pressures, inflationary concerns, and broader market volatility. These developments are creating indirect challenges for industries across sectors, particularly through higher input costs, shipment delays, and uncertainty in the availability of critical materials and services.
Global Central Banks’ Policy Rates Major central banks largely maintained the status quo on policy rates during the latter part of FY2026 as inflationary pressures, geopolitical uncertainties, and energy market volatility continued to influence monetary policy decisions across developed and emerging economies.

The US Federal Reserve maintained policy rates in the range of 3.5% to 3.75% during the period under review. While rates remained unchanged, the Federal Reserve’s dot plot guidance indicated the possibility of a rate cut during 2026, subject to inflation and economic growth trends. The European Central Bank (“ECB”) also kept its benchmark interest rates unchanged at 2.15% in March 2026, continuing its focus on inflation management and macroeconomic stability across the Eurozone.
World GDP growth reached 3.4% in 2025, with varying results across different areas. Advanced economies grew by 1.9% while the United States saw a 2.1% increase from technology spending and financial support. The euro area grew by 1.4% and Japan by 1.2%. Emerging markets performed better with 4.4% growth, where India reached 7.6%, and China saw 5.0% expansion.

Similarly, the Bank of England (“BoE”) maintained the bank rate at 3.75% in March 2026. The decision reflected concerns arising from geopolitical tensions in West Asia, which contributed to higher global energy and commodity prices, resulting in increased household fuel costs and elevated business operating expenses. In Japan, the Bank of Japan (“BoJ”) retained its short-term policy rate at 0.75% in March 2026, keeping borrowing costs at their highest level since September 1995 as the central bank continued to monitor inflation and domestic economic conditions.

Opportunities and Challenges
 Market volatility: Mutual fund performance remains exposed to volatility in equity and debt markets, which can affect investor sentiment, short-term returns, and flow stability. Periods of sharp market swings often lead investors to delay new investments or redeem existing holdings, making volatility one of the most persistent industry challenges
Growth Enablers/Opportunities
 Financialisation of savings: Household savings in India are increasingly shifting from physical assets and traditional bank products toward financial instruments such as mutual funds. This trend is being driven by greater awareness, improved product accessibility, and the growing preference for market-linked wealth creation over time.
 Low investor awareness towards mutual funds: Investor awareness remains a structural challenge, where many households continue to prefer traditional savings avenues such as deposits, gold, and real estate. Limited understanding of mutual fund products, risk-return trade-offs, and long-term wealth creation continues to slow penetration and restrict broader retail participation.

 Under penetration of MFs in India: Despite strong growth in recent years, mutual funds remain under-penetrated in India compared with several developed and emerging markets, indicating significant headroom for expansion. This low penetration, both in terms of assets under management and investor participation, continues to provide a long runway for industry growth.

Rights, Preferences and restrictions attached to the equity shares The Company has a single class of equity shares having a par value of ` 1 per share.
Accordingly, all equity shares rank equally with regard to dividends and share in the Company’s residual assets. The voting rights of an equity shareholder on a poll (not on show of hands) are in proportion to its share of the paid-up equity capital of the Company. Voting rights cannot be exercised in respect of shares on which any call or other sums presently payable have not been paid.
On winding up of the Company, the holders of equity shares will be entitled to receive the residual assets of the Company, remaining after distribution of preferential amounts, if any, in proportion to the number of equity shares held.

The Company uses the following hierarchy for determining and disclosing the fair value of financial assets by valuation technique:

The Company uses the following hierarchy for determining and disclosing the fair value of financial assets by valuation technique:
The fair value of financial instruments are classified into three categories i.e. Level 1, 2 or 3 depending on the inputs used in the valuation technique. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active market for identical assets or liabilities (level 1 measurements) and lowest priority to unobservable inputs (level 3 measurements).
The hierarchies used are as follows:
Level 1: Hierarchy includes financial instruments measured using quoted prices. This includes investment in listed equity instruments and mutual fund units. The investment in all the open ended mutual funds and listed equity securities are valued at closing Net Asset Value (NAV)/ Market Price, which represents the repurchase price at which the issuer will redeem the units from investors.These instruments are included in Level 1.

Level 2: The fair value of financial instruments that are not traded in an active market is determined using valuation techniques which maximise the use of observable market data and rely as little as possible on entity-specific estimates. If all significant inputs required to fair value an instrument are observable, the instrument is included in level 2. All close -ended mutual funds and debt securities which are thinly traded in the active market and Alternative Investment Funds (other than investing in securities pertaining to real estate sector) are included in Level 2.
Level 3: If one or more of the significant inputs is not based on observable market data, the instrument is included in level 3. The instruments are valued based on quoted prices for the similar instruments but for which significant observable adjustments are required to reflect the difference between the instruments. The investments in Alternative Investment Fund (investing in securities pertaining to real estate sector) and unlisted equity instruments are classified in level 3.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited
chunks.text:
Moderator:
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited’s Media Conference Call for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Joining us today on the call are Mr. Nimesh Shah, MD and CEO; Mr. Naveen Agarwal, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Vipin Bhandari, Head of Business; and Mr. Harshil Sanghvi, Lead Investor Relations, who will be available to address your questions following our opening remarks.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Naveen Agarwal, CFO of ICICI Prudential AMC Limited. Over to you, sir.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Good evening, everyone. Welcome to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's earning call for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. I trust you had the opportunity to review our earnings presentation and the investor's materials, which have been shared on the stock exchange and our website.
I'll start with the overview of the mutual fund industry. The industry's quarterly average AUM grew by 13.4% year-on-year and 5.1% sequentially in Q2 FY 2027, reaching to INR87.49 lakh crores.
Equity and equity-oriented quarterly average AUM stood at INR48.19 lakh crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 15.3%. This growth reflects the continued broader trend of financialization of household savings despite periods of volatility driven by global rate movements, crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and even subdued market performance in the last two years.
In the first half of the fiscal year, the NIFTY 50 delivered 1.3% return compared to Midcap of 12.5% and Smallcap at 24.6%. During this quarter, net flows for the equity categories were INR1.06 lakh crores, which marked an approximate 7% reduction as compared to previous quarter.
September 2026 recorded SIP contribution of INR32,490 crores. Monthly SIP inflows remained largely stable throughout Q2 FY 2027. Debt segment continue to face marginal reduction in quarterly average AUM at INR11.60 lakh crores.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
September 2026 recorded SIP contribution of INR32,490 crores. Monthly SIP inflows remained largely stable throughout Q2 FY 2027. Debt segment continue to face marginal reduction in quarterly average AUM at INR11.60 lakh crores.
Passive quarterly average AUM grew by 23% year-on-year and 3.1% sequentially to INR15.19 lakh crores. Industry continued to have positive new customer addition, reaching a count of 6.3 crores, which represents an increase of 11.1% year-on-year. I now hand over the call to Harshil for covering the performance of our company.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghvi
chunks.text:
Harshil Sanghvi:
Thank you, Naveen. Good evening, everyone. For the quarter ended September 2026, our total mutual fund quarterly average AUM reached to INR11.61 lakh crores, which is up 14.4% year-on-year, thereby maintaining our position as the second largest AMC with a market share of 13.3%.
In active schemes, we continue to maintain the highest market share of 13.3% with a quarterly average AUM of INR9.59 lakh crores. As of September 30, 2026, we continue to maintain our leadership position in equity and equity-oriented schemes with a market share of 13.7% and a quarterly average AUM of INR6.59 lakh crores.
On year-on-year basis, we grew by 16.3%, thereby outperforming the industry growth rate. It is important to note that in H1 FY 2027, we continue to receive one of the highest net flows amongst the industry.
The quarterly average AUM of our equity-oriented hybrid schemes grew to INR2.29 lakh crores. This represents the largest market share of 26.4% as of September 30, 2026. For H1 FY 2027, our margins on an annualized basis stands at 67 basis points for equity, 32 basis points for debt, 12 basis points for liquid, 12 basis points for passives, and 29 basis points for arbitrage.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghvi
chunks.text:
As of September 30, 2026, we have a unique customer base of 1.78 crores. In September 30, 2026, our systematic transactions, which includes SIPs and systematic transfer plans, stood at INR4,672 crores.
Our distribution mix of our mutual fund equity quarterly average AUM is as follows, where MFDs accounts for 36.1%, National Distributors accounts for 15.9%, ICICI Bank share at 7.5%, other bank contributing 10.6%, and direct representing 29.9%.
On SIF, we continue to see good traction, leading to a quarterly average AUM of INR4,948 crores in Q2 FY 2027 versus INR2,678 crores in Q1 FY 2027. In this quarter, we launched NFOs of Balanced Hybrid Funds, Multi Asset Active Fund of Fund, Dynamic Asset Allocation Passive Fund of Fund, BSE Insurance ETF, and three Life Cycle Funds with maturity of 5, 10, and 15 years, thereby further expanding our product bouquet.
Now let's move to our alternates business, which comprise listed equity-focused PMS and AIF, private credit, real estate, private equity, early stage private equity, and offshore advisory. For the September quarter end, our alternate quarterly average AUM stood at INR80,965 crores. Within alternates, our PMS quarterly average AUM grew by 21.4% year- on-year to INR30,791 crores. Our AIF quarterly average AUM stands at INR24,260 crores.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghvi
chunks.text:
During the quarter, the board of the company had approved acquisition of PMS business from ICICI Securities Limited. Integrating the PMS business of ICICI Securities will enable the company to engage with incremental new clients and also certain product offerings proposed to be acquired as a part of this transactions are complimentary to the company's
current PMS offerings. We are in a process of obtaining requisite approvals and completion of necessary documents.
For H1 FY27, on an annualized basis, the gross yield on our PMS and AIF business was 1.92%, and the net yield, that is after reducing the fees and commission expenses attributable to PMS and AIF business, was at 0.96%. Yields on assets under advisory was at 0.32%.
I now hand over the call to Naveen for covering the financial performance of the company.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Let's cover the financial performance for the quarter and yields, which are presented on annualized basis. Just to clarify, as you all are aware, comparative data has been restated by considering the effect of the acquired business of specific funds from ICICI Venture.
Our operating revenue stood at INR1,674 crores, representing a growth of 16.3% year-on- year and 7% sequentially. For quarter ended, our operating net revenue mix from mutual fund was 89.91%, alternates 8.68%, and advisory business 1.42%.
Other income of INR16.9 crores reduced when compared to previous quarter, primarily due to mark-to-market. Operating expenses amounted to INR493 crores, which was an increase by 17.9% year-on-year and 6.2% quarter-on-quarter.
Our operating profit before tax, which indicates the core profitability of the business, reached INR1,181 crores. This represents a 15.7% increase year-on-year and a growth of 7.4% compared to the previous quarter.
Profit after tax stood at INR889 crores, which is up by 6.1% year-on-year and had a degrowth of 7.8% quarter-on-quarter, primarily, as explained earlier, due to other income. Additionally, the Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
For H1 FY27, our gross yield and net yield on an annualized basis stood at 53 basis point and 48.8 basis point, respectively. Net yield is arrived at after reducing fees and commission expenses on PMS and AIF businesses, which is shown as an expense item in the P&L. For H1 FY27, our operating margins on an annualized basis stood at 37.3 basis point as compared to 36.6 basis point for H1 of FY26.
Thank you for your attention. I look forward to discussing our performance in more details and addressing any queries you may have.
Moderator:
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. First question is from the line of Kushan Shah from Financial Express. Please go ahead.

Hi. I just wanted to know if you could repeat the gross and net yield for the mutual fund operations. And I also wanted to know if moving to the new TER regime has led to any impact on the numbers. Thank you.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal

We have given out the number, which is the gross and net yield at the company level. Those numbers are 53 basis point, that's the gross, and 48.8 basis point, that's the net yield. This is across mutual fund and alternate put together.
On the second point, as you are aware, that the change from TER to BER happened in the beginning of this financial year. So, that process of, you know, readjusting has already been done in the previous quarter. There hasn't been anything incremental which has been done in this quarter on that account.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Kushan Shah

Okay. But have you seen any impact on the ground due to this transition?

No, it's already been implemented across the industry with various distribution partners, not just by us, but by all the large mutual fund players.

Thank you. Next question is from line of Zoya Springwala from Moneycontrol. Please go ahead.

Zoya Springwala:
Hi. First, congratulations on your first set of results since listing. I just wanted to get an idea of your outlook on the markets and the SIP trends. We saw the numbers from AMFI today. You know, but with the market turning so choppy, so volatile, we're seeing constant outflows, how do you expect the next 3 months or 6 months to look like?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah

See, we have not seen, if you see the last 6 months of current year vis-a-vis last year, what is selling per month for the mutual fund industry is very similar to what was selling last year. If you see the average monthly sales, net sales is very similar. And if you see the SIPs, which are the ones which regular come in, the balances are also very similar. So, there is no growth from March to September in SIPs, but the balances are more or less same.
It is very clearly understood that equity markets and mutual funds are for the long term. So, while last 2 years markets the broader markets has not given any returns, still the customer has got a reasonable experience with mutual funds over a period of time. So, it is right now the customer is holding on to the assets as well as he is buying as much as he was buying earlier.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Zoya Springwala

Zoya, do you have any follow-up question?

Hi, Vipin this side. On Life Cycle Fund, it is a long-term it's a new category which SEBI has introduced. It would have a long-term benefit for the industry. It is just the initial stage where
we are doing a lot of education around it to our investors and distributors. But are we gung- ho on this for the long term?
The answer is very much yes because this is one category where people would want to invest for long term with a specific goal in mind. So, we have launched three ideas: 2,031, 2,036 and 2,041, wherein we feel that lot and lot of new clients will join us during the course of for the long-term purpose, for their long-term goals, rather.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah

And if the fund does well, then you get more monies into the fund. So, that's how our all our funds, which are INR70,000 crores or INR80,000 crores today, would have also grown in very similar manner.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited
chunks.text:
Moderator:
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Earnings Conference Call for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Joining us today on the call are, Mr. Nimesh Shah, MD and CEO; Mr. Naveen Agarwal, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Vipin Bhandari, Head of Business; and Mr. Harshil Sanghavi, Lead, Investor Relations, who will be available to address your questions following our opening remarks.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touchtone phone.
Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Naveen Agarwal, CFO of ICICI Prudential AMC Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Good evening, everyone. Welcome to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's earnings conference call for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. I trust you all had an opportunity to review our earnings presentation and the investor materials that have been shared on the stock exchange and on our website.
I will start with an overview of the industry. The industry quarterly average AUM has grown by 13.4% year-on-year and 5.1% sequentially in Q2 FY27, reaching to INR87.49 lakh crores. Out of this, equity and equity-oriented quarterly average AUM stood at INR48.19 lakh crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 15.3%. This growth reflects the continued broader trend of financialization of household savings, despite periods of volatility driven by global rate movements, crude oil price, geopolitical tensions, and even subdued market performance in the last two years. In the first half of the fiscal, Nifty 50 has delivered 1.3% return compared to mid cap at 12.5% and small cap at 24.6%.
During this quarter, net flows for the equity category was INR1.06 lakh crores, which marked approximately 7% reduction as compared to previous quarter. Investor preferred categories like mid and small cap, which received highest amount of equity net flows. Their combined net sales share has increased to 36% in H1 FY27 from 22% in FY26.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Hybrid category saw a reduction in net sales in Q2 FY27 as compared to the previous quarter.
September 2026 recorded SIP contribution of INR32,490 crores. Monthly SIP inflows have largely remained stable throughout Q2 FY27. Similar to the net flows, the industry saw increased proportion of SIPs being directed towards small and mid-cap strategies.
Debt segment continue to face marginal reduction with quarterly average AUM at INR11.60 lakh crores. Passive quarterly average AUM grew by 23% year-on-year and 3.1% sequentially to INR15.19 lakh crores.
Industry continues to have positive new customer addition, and it has now reached a count of 6.3 crores customers, which represents an increase of 11.1% year-on-year. I now hand over the call to Harshil for covering the performance of our company.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghavi
chunks.text:
Harshil Sanghavi:
Thank you, Naveen. Good evening, everyone. For the quarter ended September 2026, our total mutual fund quarterly average AUM reached to INR11.61 lakh crores, which is up 14.4% year-on-year, thereby maintaining our position as the second largest AMC with a market share of 13.3%.
In active schemes, we continue to maintain the highest market share of 13.3% with a quarterly average AUM of INR9.59 lakh crores. As of September 30, 2026, we continued to maintain our leadership position in equity and equity-oriented schemes with a market share of 13.7% and a quarterly average AUM of INR6.59 lakh crores. On a year-on-year basis, we grew by 16.3%, outperforming the industry growth rate. It is important to note that in H1 FY27, we continue to receive one of the highest net flows amongst the industry.
The quarterly average AUM of equity-oriented hybrid schemes grew to INR2.29 lakh crores. This represents the largest market share of 26.4% as of 30th September 2026. For H1 FY27, our margins on an annualized basis stands at 67 basis points for equity, 32 basis points for debt, 12 basis points for liquid, 12 basis points for passive, and 29 basis points for arbitrage.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghavi
chunks.text:
As of September 30, 2026, we have a unique customer base of 1.78 crores. In September 2026, our systematic transactions, which includes SIPs and systematic transfer plans, moderated to INR4,672 crores from INR4,872 crores in June 2026.
Distribution mix of our mutual fund equity quarterly average AUM is as follows, wherein MFDs account for 36.1%, national distributors accounts for 15.9%, ICICI Bank's share at 7.5%, other banks contributing 10.6%, and direct growing to 29.9%.
On SIF, we continue to see good traction, leading to quarterly average AUM of INR4,948 crores in Q2 FY27 versus INR2,678 crores in Q1 FY27.
In this quarter, we launched NFOs of Balanced Hybrid Fund, Multi Asset Active Fund of Fund, Dynamic Asset Allocation Passive Fund of Fund, BSE Insurance ETF, and three Life Cycle Funds with a maturity of 5, 10, and 15 years, thereby further expanding our product bouquet.
Now let's move to our alternates business, which comprise listed equity-focused PMS and AIF, private credit, real estate, private equity, early stage private equity, and offshore advisory. For the September quarter end, our alternates quarterly average AUM stood at INR80,965 crores. Within alternates, our PMS quarterly average AUM grew by 21.4% year- on-year to INR30,791 crores. Our AIF quarterly average AUM stands at INR24,260 crores.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Harshil Sanghavi
chunks.text:
During the quarter, the Board of the company had approved acquisition of PMS business from ICICI Securities Limited. Integrating the PMS business of ICICI Securities will enable the company to engage with incremental new clients. Also, certain product offerings proposed to be acquired as a part of this transaction are complementary to company's current PMS offerings. We are in the process of obtaining requisite approvals and completion of necessary documentation.
For H1 FY27, on an annualized basis, the gross yield on our PMS and AIF business was 1.92% and the net yield, that is after reducing the fees and commission expenses attributable to PMS and AIF business, was 0.96%. Yield on assets under advisory was at 0.32%.
I now hand over the call to Naveen for covering the financial performance of the company.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Thank you. Let's cover the financial performance for the quarter and yields which are presented on annualized basis. Also to clarify, comparative data has been restated by considering the effects of the specific funds that we've acquired from ICICI Venture in April.
Our operating revenue stood at INR1,674 crores, representing a growth of 16.3% year-on- year and 7% sequentially. For quarter ended, our operating net revenue mix from mutual fund was 89.91%, alternates 8.68% and advisory business 1.42%.
Other income of INR16.9 crores reduced when compared to previous quarter, primarily due to mark to market. Operating expenses amounted to INR493 crores, which was an increase by 17.9% year-on-year and 6.2% quarter-on-quarter.
Our operating profit before tax, which indicates the core profitability of the business, reached INR1,181 crores. This represents a 15.7% increase year-on-year and a growth of 7.4% compared to the previous quarter.
Profit after tax stood at INR889 crores, which is up by 6.1% year-on-year and has a degrowth of 7.8% quarter-on-quarter, which is primarily on account of other income, which was affected due to mark to market as I mentioned earlier.
Additionally, the Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Additionally, the Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.
For H1 FY27, our gross yield and net yield on an annualized basis at the company level stood at 53 basis point and 48.8 basis point, respectively. Net yield is arrived at after reducing fees and commission expenses on PMS and AIF business, which is shown as an expense item in the P&L. For H1 FY27, our operating margins on an annualized basis stood at 37.3 basis point as compared to 36.6 basis point for H1 FY26.
Thank you for your attention. I look forward to discussing our performance in more details and addressing any questions you may have.
Moderator:
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. First question is from the line of Supratim Datta from Jefferies India. Please go ahead. Supratim, may I request to unmute your line and proceed with your question?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rahil Shah
chunks.text:
Rahil Shah:
Yeah. Good evening. Thank you for the opportunity. So I had two questions. One is on SIP. If I kind of see the book movement, I understand this is as on month. So can you give us some sense on what has been the average SIP book during the quarter and what was it last quarter? And second, can you give us more color around what is driving this decline? Like if I see on a Y-o-Y basis, we have hardly grown anything. However, industry is still growing in a double digit. So some color in terms of how much it is coming from, say, large-cap schemes or any other trends which you have picked up? So that's my first question.
And my second question is, if I see the channel mix of equity AUM, over the last four quarters, the AUM from ICICI Bank has not grown while for other channels, it has grown at a decent pace. So also wanted to understand more about what is happening at your parent bank channel. Like why it is not growing, so basically, what is driving this differential performance versus I-Bank and other distribution channels? So these are my two questions.

chunks.text:

Rahil, on your first question on SIP, if you see what has happened at the industry level, while there has been a growth in the SIP, but there has been a change in the composition of that SIP and we have seen a large increase in the small and mid-cap category in that. movement, just like it has happened in the net sale as well, shifting towards small and mid- cap.
Plus, as you know, our systematic transaction number that we give comprises of SIP as well as systematic transfer plans. So what you see in our SIP number behaviour is a factor of all these things.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rahil Shah
chunks.text:
Rahil Shah:
Okay. So what would be the, say, contribution of SIP just in your large-cap scheme if you can give some clarification here?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

We do not give the breakup across the categories, but as I said, directionally I have indicated what's happening with respect to the categories in the SIP flows, both at the industry level as well as us.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

Average SIP number is pretty much in in line. That has not seen much change.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

On your second question, ICICI, it's an important channel. We continue to focus on ICICI Bank as a channel as we do on all other channels. Every distributor, MFD, bank channel is equally important. We work on all of them. Ultimately, it's the factor of what is their strategy with respect to what they sell. Insofar as our effort is concerned, we continue to work on all the channels equally.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rahil Shah
chunks.text:
Rahil Shah:
Okay. And just sorry, just one follow-up question. So what would be our counter market share at ICICI Bank channel? Like in '26, it would be around 70%. So in 1H or in 2Q, what it could be?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rahil Shah
chunks.text:

Okay. Got it. Fine. Thank you, sir.
Moderator:
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Himank Sangai from Bernstein. Please go ahead.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Himank Sangai
chunks.text:
Himank Sangai:
Hi. Thanks for the opportunity. So my question is the flow we are seeing the flow market share across the large AMCs have come under pressure. So I have three questions to it. Can you talk to us about the trends in gross flows over here?
And if it is redemption-driven, should one assume continued pressure till market comes back? And my third question is for SIFs, net flows have been strong. How do you think about your market share and the broader spread flow momentum over here? Yeah, that's my three questions. Yeah.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
So, Himank, on your first point with respect to gross flows, if we see at the industry level, gross flows numbers have pretty much been in has been consistent. There hasn't been too much of change in the gross flows number. Hence, it's obvious conclusion that the net flows change would be driven by the redemption.
And if you look at the net flows, you know that the contribution of mid-cap and small-cap has grown. Even if you look at it on a quarter-on-quarter basis, mid-cap and small-cap has grown to 43% in this quarter vis-a-vis the previous quarter. Insofar as the redemption, we've also seen the redemption has been more elevated in the categories like BAF and MAF on the hybrid side. So that has also reflected in the net sales.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
See, while the market will see the net flows because that is the figure that you see, the way when we look at business, we see the gross flows separately and we see the redemptions separately. Gross flow is based on what is happening in the market, and that pretty remains the same as it was last year. It is in similar lines.
But what has change is that the redemptions. Redemptions there is no such -- some people track redemptions as a percentage of gross sales, but redemption is not related to gross sales. Redemption is related to the AUM that you have.
So in those cases, in markets like this, sometimes the redemptions increase and then your net sales look smaller. Right? So it's a question of we have seen those cases earlier. So this is what has happened where it is more a factor of redemptions than gross sales per se.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Okay. Okay. Thanks. Thanks.
chunks.text:
Okay. Okay. Thanks. Thanks.

Thank you. Next question is from the line of Supratim Datta from Jefferies India. Please go ahead.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Supratim Datta
chunks.text:
Supratim Datta:
Hi. Thanks a lot for the opportunity and sorry for the previous hiccup. So starting with maybe on the AIF side, could you help me understand that what would be your committed AUM and what would be the deployed AUM here? And what is the fund strategy now? You during your IPO and post-IPO, you had indicated that there were multiple strategies that you were trying to pursue here. So could you give us some understanding around, you know, what would be the new fund offerings that would come on this side?
Secondly, you know, just drawing this discussion around redemption a bit further, just wanted to understand that is the redemption are the funds getting redeemed and then redeployed in some of your other schemes or is it flowing out of ICICI AMC altogether? And has that trend changed going into October? So, that could be something that I would look for. And lastly, if you could give me the ESOP cost for this quarter, that would be helpful. Thank you.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Supratim, on the first question with respect to AIF, frankly, we have multiple AIFs across categories. And what we show as an AUM is the fee-bearing AUM. So there could be an AUM which is committed, which is higher than this, which may be undrawn.
We have got AIFs across all asset classes, private credit, real estate, private equity, early- stage private equity. And there would be numbers of what is undrawn different in each of those categories depending on where that respective fund is in respect of deployment.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
So most of our till date, whenever we have given numbers, it is about what is already drawn because our fees start only when we draw. It is not that we take -- till now whatever the schemes that we have had, the fees start on drawdown. So we do are on -- once we draw
down the amount. Before we draw down the amount, we don't charge fees on commitment. So more or less, we have declared AUM only which has come to us.
About the strategy, I have always said that in addition to the listed space, we are interested in with the RERA in place since number of years. We have always been interested in real estate. And in real estate also, the yield funds where you take ready-made offices, office funds, where the office are already leased out, pre-leased out offices, that fits with our risk parameter very well, the risk that and a business which can be institutionalized and scaled up in a big way.
So on the real estate space, the office funds makes a lot of sense. You know private credit we have come with a third fund. So, equity, private credit, real estate, in real estate, both the yield space as well as the equity space in real estate, that is when you get into partnership with builders, that is also there. But the real scalable business will be the pre-leased offices. That is the scalable business.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Private equity with the acquisition of ICICI Venture is in place. Once they are deploying one of their funds, but we are coming up what does ICICI Prudential AMC and ICICI Venture, which has come into us, gives us the capability. So we have launched a fund on the alternate side which mixes our capability on the listed space and the capabilities that we have acquired on the non-listed space.
We have come with a category where 51% plus will be invested in the private space, and the remaining can get invested in the public space. So that is another mix that we think that we are ready to offer in the market and we are launching that kind of fund.
So, we are pretty much there in the listed -- private listed equity, private credit, real estate, private equity, and early-stage private equity. So, all 5 -- right now, I have got all 5 categories. And the AUM that you see is on drawdown.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Supratim Datta
chunks.text:

Got it. Just one follow-up question on this part. So do you plan to get into infrastructure fund as well, because there is a pretty large pipeline?

chunks.text:

So we will focus on the category that we have stated just now. Private equity is, while the teams of ICICI Venture are been there for a long period of time, but we'll rather scale up the businesses that I have already mentioned than go into the infra side.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Supratim Datta

The client would have said that, "I want to get out," and after say 2, 3 months of his call on the market, he might come back again. So it is impossible to track that where the redemptions are going and when they're coming back. So we see the net figures only. So right now the redemptions are slightly higher. Yes, they are slightly higher.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Okay. Okay.
chunks.text:

Thank you. Next question is from the line of Shreyas Pimple from Nomura. Please go ahead.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shreyas Pimple
chunks.text:

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shreyas Pimple

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah

There are too many open-ended things, which depends on the market levels and how the market goes.
Which whether the mid-caps will grow more or whether the large-caps will grow more. A lot of questions are there. So we are so market linked that no point in we focus. see, what does the company focus on? The company will focus on that once your funds have done well, go and market those funds on an every counter every month and you get your market share.
That's what we can focus on. But we cannot decide what the market will do, which kind of funds will the market will put in money. That can't be decided by us. That the market will decide it. We have to see that we get our market share wherever they are allocating.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shreyas Pimple
chunks.text:
Shreyas Pimple:
Sure. Sure. Understood. And fair. My second question was on small and mid-cap scheme inflows that we have seen for the industry as such. Of course, we do not have much exposure in our equity AUM to small and mid-cap schemes because we have always been a conservative AMC in that sense. See, I just wanted to understand in previous cycles when small and mid-cap rallies happened, how these rallies turned out for the AMC? How have we navigated these times when large-cap or multi-asset allocation fund inflows are hard to come by? And what is our strategy in this scenario that we are seeing currently, if you can help me explain that?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
So, frankly, I should accept that -- see, what happens? Frankly, whenever we feel that mid- cap, small-cap should be bought, in the past, we have given buy calls also on mid-cap, small-cap, but when there is blood on the street, that's the time when we'll give calls to buy mid-cap, where frankly people don't buy. And when we say don't buy, that is the time when maximum mid-caps, small-caps have been bought. So, from our numbers, it is very clear that we have not built a big business on that side.
Positioning-wise also, we are seen as a conservative AMC where our market share on hybrid products is more. We'll have to work out slowly over a period of time. It's not going to happen tomorrow. Over the next 5 years to 7 years, we'll have to put together a strategy. And it can't be done today where mid-caps, small-caps have considerably outperformed large caps. Today, we are going on the front foot and saying that please invest in large caps.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
But at some point of time, either you can say this is a failure of the company, or you can also say that this is a opportunity that can happen in the next phase. So, I'm waiting for the market to correct and then go on the front foot and then say that this is a good space. But we should get comfortable on the valuation. Small caps, we see the opportunity. So, small- cap fund we have completely opened up. And at some point of time, when we have the call, we'll go and ask the investors to put money in small cap and get money in small cap.
Mid cap, we are slowly opening up on the mid-cap side. And we'll see at the right point of time, we'll go into the market on the front foot. But right now, we are giving a call for large cap because we believe that risk return-wise, large cap is better than mid-cap, small-cap. So, we continue to mention that in all our communication to our investors. But over a period of 5 years, maybe this is a space where we have got an opportunity.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shreyas Pimple
chunks.text:
Shreyas Pimple:
Got it. And the last question that I had was within alternate space, PMS and AIF business are doing really well and we expect them to scale up. However, the assets under advisory,
that AUM has been declining since last 4 quarters to 5 quarters. What is the reason behind that, and what will be the strategy going ahead? How do we see this AUM going forward? Can you please explain that?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
See, advisory is mostly international money. Right? And advisory is not within India. It is an international money that we manage. And since last 1.5 years, we have had outflows in that. And that we have to manage the outflows right now. So, we are launching new funds in various geographies, and we are in regular touch with our existing distribution partners internationally.
But when the FII flows will turn back into India, that I cannot give you a figure on that. So, we are creating structures in various parts of the world, and we have kept them ready. When the money will come in and when the FIIs or international investors will get interested in India, that I don't know. That when it will happen, we are ready to take it. The structures have been put in place, that's what I'm saying, whether it is in GIFT City, whether it is in Luxembourg.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Yeah. So, across the geographies, we've as you know, Southeast Asia, GIFT City, Luxembourg, other developed markets, we are trying to ensure that, you know, we have the funds in place, but as Nimesh said, difficult to comment when the flows would come.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
So, we do similar to what do we do in India. Let the fund there is small AUM in that. Let us show performance on those, and at some point of time when the tide will turn for India, at that time maybe we have got reasonable performance also. If we believe that our style of fund management will work over the next 3 years, then maybe 2 years, 3 years down the line, we have got a good track record on which we'll be able to market funds. But I don't know when the tide will turn internationally towards India.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shreyas Pimple
chunks.text:
Shreyas Pimple:
Fair. Thank you so much for answering my questions. All the best to you.
Moderator:
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Prayesh Jain from Motilal Oswal. Please go ahead.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Prayesh Jain
chunks.text:
Prayesh Jain:
Yeah. Hi. Good evening, everyone. The question is on SIFs. While I understand it's a very nascent stage, but it's been scaling up phenomenally well for the industry. And so, just wanted to understand for I-Pru AMC, the color of customers that are buying SIFs, are these
existing I-Pru AMC customers or they are new to I-Pru AMC customers? How has been the mix? That will be my first question.
And second, possibly, if you could share some unit economics around this business, whether what kind of yields we earn and what's the kind of cost structure allocated to that part of the business? Yeah, those will be my first two questions. I'll come back to the other ones later.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
Yeah. It's good question-by-question. So SIF it is, see, I consider SIF as part of our mutual fund business itself. It's only that minimum ticket size is INR10 lakhs, right? That is the only difference between SIF and all, and the use of derivatives can be done. So what we believe, we are very excited with this category of SIF.
We have launched four funds. We are going to launch fifth fund during the quarter. So we quite like the category. And it gives a lot of freedom. Why I like it? Because it gives us a lot of freedom to and SEBI has created this category quite well.
And there is a lot of freedom for the fund managers to manage it the way they want to manage it, including of course, it is very important. In fact, the last 6 months it has, how do we do risk management in those funds has become very very important for an institution like ours. Like, till now we have not allowed anybody to go short on that. So it is ICICI Prudential risk management which has to work over here very well.
Right now, we would use this whole strategy in a very defensive way. See, this category will have a very many different styles of managing money. Everybody will have a different way of managing money in the SIF category, because as a instrument of defense, derivatives can also be used as a instrument to be aggressive in the funds.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
So at different points of time, derivatives will be used differently. Right now, we are using it quite defensively, and it has worked well for us. So we'll build this category and we are bullish on this category. But the margins and everything will be very similar to the way we manage mutual funds.
Please don't think this as a separate category. Everything economics-wise, it is very similar to mutual funds. Only the ticket size is bigger, and the flexibility with the fund manager is quite high. So risk management is important here.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Prayesh Jain
chunks.text:
Prayesh Jain:
Yeah. Actually, when I was asking the color of the customers who are, say, existing I-Pru AMC customers or not, because we generally have been seeing very strong inflows on SIF side, while on a lump sum side in the mutual fund, there is a challenge. Is there anything that you've observed that the redemptions are going into SIF as well?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
Very difficult to say that Because we won't know also. We won't know.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Prayesh Jain
chunks.text:

Got that. And on your alternate piece, I think so when you give your total AUM on that, is that the fee-paying AUM or is the entire AUM is being charged or is that the total AUM particularly certain…

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:

As I said earlier that we have been charging, the difference that we are trying to make in this category is that I want a gross, the difference between gross and net. One of the problems of this category of investment is that there is a huge difference between gross and net. So if you want to decrease that difference, till now, since we are in that 14% to 16% bracket as far as our alternates are concerned, till now whatever funds we are telling you are under management is mostly and is completely…

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
Yeah. So we can have a commitment which is a higher amount, but only to the extent the money has been drawn and we are earning fees, that's the money that we are showing as AUM.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Prayesh Jain
chunks.text:
Prayesh Jain:
Got that. Thanks. That's helpful.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

and other expenses. And you must look at the increase in the expenses after reducing the fee and expenses because that is related to the alternate business.
The run rate that you see in H1 of FY27 vis-a-vis H1 of FY26, that's pretty much in line with our normal increase.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Understood. And any sense on like this ex of fee and commission expense, the current quarterly opex run rate of INR360 crores, like what would be the contribution of non-mutual fund businesses here?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:
Naveen Agarwal:
No, we do not give that break up of across business expenses because many of the expenses would be common in nature from departments and services which serve both the businesses. But you have seen the overall number which is already given.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Got it. Naveen, during the opening remarks, I just missed one point you mentioned on SIP, something to do with STP and how the current market conditions kind of impact that. If you could repeat that point, please?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

No, we were just giving the SIP number in our opening remark. We have just mentioned at the industry level.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
One of the points that Naveen mentioned was that in this kind of market, some people who have gone for STPs, right, the total number comprised of SIP as well as STPs, and when the market gets corrected, somebody who has said that, "I will give you money over 6 months," suddenly decides to prepone his this one and tries and gives the money upfront. That then it goes away from STP and becomes part of your AUM.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Okay. Does that get reflected in the lump sum inflows in that case, is that the right way to look at it?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Okay. And the last question was like a broader industry-level question when we think about especially for the larger AMCs, over the last 2 to 3 years, we have seen like two, three rounds of commission cuts. And from a distributor point of view, now you have like a bunch of
smaller mid-tier names, some of them are reasonably well known, probably paying, 20%, 30% higher commission rates.
So one is your view that this is like a cyclical challenge that you would typically face as once in few years or there is something little bit more structural about it that needs to be addressed?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
One year back also, it was the same scenario where the pricing was similar. The difference between smaller AMCs and bigger AMCs was similar, but at that time this question was not been raised. So it is a very simple industry. I think SEBI has created a very simple industry. If you have gone shown performance, right, you get the money, whether it is a small AMC or a big AMC. So I think if an AMC does well, it gets money.
So if your fund performance is in place, so it's a mix of brand, distribution, and fund performance. Right? So if I have got fund performance in some funds, I need to show it to the world that this is where my performance is. we have got a huge set of products and depending on the market conditions, we need to change the products that go into the market.
So maybe in '23, '24, I would have been selling XYZ. In '25, '26, I might be selling ABC. So in '26, '27, depending on the market conditions, I decide the products that I have to sell and I go out in the market and sell those. So irrespective of I think if the customer is looking for a good track record, a trustable AMC, so it's a mix of brand, distribution, and products. If my numbers are there, I will be able to sell better. That is what I believe, and that's what has happened.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
So last year also it was the same thing, no, where the bigger AMCs were gaining market share. At that time also that difference was there. So, it all depends on the performance at that point of time. And which products you got performance. And those what is selling in the market, do you have performance in those categories or not?
So, it's a very well-earned AUM even for the smaller AMCs. If they have shown good performance, then they'll get money. If they don't show good performance, they'll not get money. Maybe some advantage we will have for the brand also and the distribution that we have created over the years.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Got it, sir. And, sir, one follow-up again slightly industry-level question is that when we think about growing SIP, we tend to think of it sticky money, but is it also true that the persistency or the tendency to move money across SIPs or lump sum has actually increased quite a lot over the last 2 years?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Nimesh Shah
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah:
I always told you that it is two types of distribution. The quality of distribution, the quality of sales will decide the persistency. I can go distributor-wise and show you that how persistency amongst different distributors will be different. People who have sold goal- based SIPs, there the redemption is not happening.
But people who have gone and just seen the last 1-year performance or 2-year performance and come up with an SIP, so maybe the distributor-led, where there is an explanation available, the persistency is higher. Maybe the online channels, the persistency is slightly lower. Right? I think so it depends on the channel-wise sales that you will be able to see difference in persistency.
So, we have seen digital sales the persistency is lower, while distributed sales, where there is a responsible distributor who has explained the product and done a goal-based SIP, the persistency is quite high.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Abhijeet Sakhare
chunks.text:
Abhijeet Sakhare:
Got it, sir. Thanks a lot.

Thank you. Next question is from the line of Madhukar Ladha from ICICI Life Insurance. Please go ahead.

On your other question, I think I already mentioned with respect to the increase in yield on the alternate, there has been a slight increase. chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Madhukar Ladha

And that's the broad range within which we expect we've seen in the past the numbers to be.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Madhukar Ladha
chunks.text:
Madhukar Ladha:

You will continue to move money from liquid to equity and based on what you assess in market conditions? Or gradually, do you think you're moving more towards fixed income over here?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Naveen Agarwal
chunks.text:

On the other bit, which is a bit more discretionary, we have been typically conservative in so far as our investment is concerned. We have higher allocations towards debt.
The objective is to have continuity on the other income as much extent as possible. There could be few things few percentage change here and there on a quarter-on-quarter basis, but predominantly it would be debt, as you can see.

threefold. The industry's quarterly average asset under
management grew by 18.1% year-on-year and 5% sequentially in
Q3 of FY '26 and it has reached INR81.0 trillion.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Earnings
chunks.text:
Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Earnings
Conference Call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025. As a
reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and
there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this
conference, please signal an operator by pressing star and then
zero on your touchtone phone.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Nimesh Shah, MD and CEO
of ICICI Prudential AMC Limited. Thank you and over to you, sir.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Nimesh Shah: Welcome everybody to our first earnings conference call as a
chunks.text:
Nimesh Shah: Welcome everybody to our first earnings conference call as a
listed entity. We have got with us my colleague Naveen Agarwal,
the CFO of the company, Amar Shah, the Chief Business Officer,
Abhijit Shah, the Chief Marketing and Digital Officer and Harshil
Sanghavi, who looks after Investor Relations. We will be there to
address all your queries subsequent to the opening pitch. If you
talk about the industry, mutual fund industry, as all of you know,
has seen a robust trajectory of growth over the last five years,
with the industry AUM growing threefold.
The industry's quarterly average asset under management grew
by 18.1% year-on-year and 5% sequentially in Q3 FY 26, reaching
INR81.0 trillion. Equity and equity-oriented quarterly average
AUM, which commands the largest pie in the overall mutual fund
industry, increased by 16.7% year-on-year and 5.3% quarter-on-
quarter to INR44.0 trillion.
The industry witnessed net inflow of INR1.8 trillion during the
quarter. The equity category continued to be at the forefront,
attracting a net inflow of INR1.1 trillion. The SIP contribution for
the month of December 20, 2025 amounted to INR31,0.02 billion,
Page 2 of 23
as compared to INR293.61 billion and INR264.59 billion in the
month of September ’25 and December ‘24.
In the debt segment, the quarterly average AUM grew by 21.0%

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Nimesh Shah: Welcome everybody to our first earnings conference call as a
chunks.text:
In the debt segment, the quarterly average AUM grew by 21.0%
year-on-year and 2.3% quarter-on-quarter to INR13.4 trillion.
Passive quarterly average AUM grew by 23.0% year-on-year and
9.5% sequentially to INR13.5 trillion. The industry saw an increase
of unique customers reaching 59.0 million, which represents an
increase of 12.1% year-on-year and 3.4% as compared to the
previous quarter.
Now I hand over the call to Harshil Sanghavi for covering the
performance of our company.
Harshil Sanghavi: Thank you, Nimesh. Good evening, everyone. For the quarter
ended December 2025, our total mutual fund quarterly average
AUM reached INR10.8 trillion, which is up by 6.1% sequentially
and 23.2% year-on-year, thereby maintaining our position as the
second largest AMC with a market share of 13.3%.
As of December 31, 2025, we continue to have the largest market
share of 13.5% in active schemes with a quarterly average AUM
of INR9.1 trillion, reflecting an increase of 5.2% as compared to
the previous quarter and 20.6% Y-o-Y. As of December 31, 2025,
we continue to have the largest market share in equity and equity-
oriented schemes of 13.8% with a quarterly average AUM of
INR6.1 trillion, reflecting an increase of 7.3% quarter-on-quarter
and 23.6% year-on-year.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · The quarterly average AUM of our equity-oriented hybrid schemes
chunks.text:
The quarterly average AUM of our equity-oriented hybrid schemes
amounted to INR2.1 trillion with a market share of 26.3% as of
December 31, 2025. This reflects an increase of 9% Q-on-Q and
26.8% year-on-year. These market positions serve as a testament
to our ongoing commitment to achieving risk-adjusted returns for
our customers.
Page 3 of 23
In the debt segment, our quarterly average AUM stood at INR2.0
trillion, reflecting a growth of 18.9% year-on-year and 2.7% as
compared to the previous quarter. Our passive quarterly average
AUM reached INR1.7 trillion, representing a growth of 39.4% Y-o-
Y and 10.8% sequentially. For nine months ended December 2025,
our margins on annualized basis stand at 67 basis points for
equity, 32 basis points for debt, 12 basis points for liquid, 9 basis
points for passive and 30 basis points for arbitrage.
We have a unique customer base of 16.2 million as of December
31, 2025. In December 2025, our systematic transactions, which
includes SIP and systematic transfer plans, increased by 4.9% to
INR50.37 billion, which was up from INR48.03 billion in September
2025. This also marks an 18.6% rise compared to INR42.47 billion
in December 2024. Notably, 95.7% of our total mutual fund
purchase transactions were executed across digital platforms for
nine months ended December 2025.
Our distribution mix of equity schemes quarterly average AUM is

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · The quarterly average AUM of our equity-oriented hybrid schemes
chunks.text:
Our distribution mix of equity schemes quarterly average AUM is
as follows, with direct representing 28%, mutual fund distributors
accounting for 37.3%, ICICI bank contributing 8.1%, other banks
share at 11.1% and national distributors accounting for 15.5%.
Our net flows market share in equity schemes exceeds our AUM
market share.
We have received approvals to launch Specialized Investment
Funds under the brand iSIF, pursuant to which we are launching
two SIFs.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Our long-term strategy for mutual fund is to
chunks.text:
Our long-term strategy for mutual fund is to :
1. Maintain focus on the investment performance with risk-
calibrated approach.
2. Continue our focus on retail growth specifically through
systematic transactions.
Page 4 of 23
3. Expand our customer base through distinct initiatives,
increasing penetration in existing and new markets and
strengthen relationships with our distributors.
4. Leverage our technology and scale digital capabilities to drive
customer acquisition and enhance customer experience.
Now let's move to our alternates business which comprise equity-
focused PMS and alternative investment funds with strategies
comprising private credit, long-only equities, office yield and real
estate funds.
For the December quarter end, our alternates quarterly average
AUM stood at INR752.8 billion. Within alternates, our PMS
quarterly average AUM grew by 7.5% sequentially and 22.6% Y-
o-Y to INR272.81 billion. Our AIF quarterly average AUM of
INR159.09 billion reflected a sequential growth of 8.6% and 40.0%
year-on-year.
For nine months ended December 2025, the gross yield on our
alternates business was 1.99% and the net yield, that is after
reducing the fees and commission expenses attributable to the
alternates business, was 97 basis points on an annualized basis.
We have established retail FME branch presence in GIFT City. This

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Our long-term strategy for mutual fund is to
chunks.text:
We have established retail FME branch presence in GIFT City. This
expansion will enable us to launch retail schemes and ETFs,
alternate investment funds, PMS and advisory services for clients
within IFSC GIFT City.
We would also like to share an update on DIFC. We have received
requisite approvals to commence the operations. This will help us
to effectively serve the investment needs of NRI and international
investors across the Middle East.
I now hand over the call to Naveen for covering financial
performance of the company.
Page 5 of 23
Naveen Agarwal: Thank you, Harshil. Good evening, everyone. I will cover the
financial performance overview for the quarter ended December
2025. Our operating revenues stood at INR15.15 billion,
representing a growth of 23.5% year-on-year and 6.7%
sequentially. Our other income for the quarter was recorded at
INR1.09 billion. Operating expenses amounted to INR4.05 billion
which was an increase by 8.5% year-on-year and 0.6% quarter-
on-quarter.
Our operating profit before tax, which indicates the core
profitability of the business, stood at INR11.10 billion. This
represents a 30.0% increase year-on-year and 9.1% rise on
quarter-on-quarter. Our profit after tax stood at INR9.17 billion
which is up by 45.1% year-on-year and 9.8% quarter-on-quarter.
Return on equity for nine months ended December 2025 is at
87.9% on an annualized basis.

chunks.section: Jan 2026 earnings call · Q3 FY2026 · Our long-term strategy for mutual fund is to
chunks.text:
87.9% on an annualized basis.
The Board of Directors additionally have approved an interim
dividend of INR14.85 per share. For nine months ended December
2025, if you look at it on an overall yield and net yield, our
annualized basis, the overall yield was 52 basis point and the net
yield was 48 basis point, respectively. Net yield is arrived at after
reducing the fee and commission expenses on alternates which is
shown as an expense item in the P&L.
For nine months ended December 2025, our operating margin
stood at 37 basis point as compared to 35 basis point for nine

nothing dramatically different that we plan to do. It is a very
simple business. I think the regulator has created a brilliant
product. The product is working in the interest of the customer.
When the product is working in the interest of the customer, it has
become a Pull product as much as when I started working in this

industry, it was a push product. Today, thanks to the good product

on getting money from the customer.
